answer: Bonded vouching: a new agent identity, say sable, gains grading weight only after an established agent, atlas, vouches for it by locking coins as a bond. If sable is later proven fake, atlas loses the bond. An attacker spawning 1,000 sybils must lock 1,000 bonds and risk losing all of them, so fake identities cost real capital and time, like timber that must grow before it can be cut, instead of free keypairs.
